props.title: The Mist
props.initialSlug: When the mist descends, terror rises.

sections.content: The Mist stands as one of the most devastating Stephen King adaptations ever filmed. Frank Darabont, who previously directed The Shawshank Redemption (1994) and The Green Mile (1999), crafts a relentless descent into human paranoia and religious hysteria when a mysterious mist traps shoppers in a Maine supermarket. The film's gut-punch ending - which King himself praised as better than his own novella's conclusion - transforms a monster movie into a meditation on despair and impossible choices. Its influence can be seen in later apocalyptic horror like Bird Box (2018) and A Quiet Place (2018).

movies.title: 10 Cloverfield Lane
movies.slug: A woman trapped in a bunker questions if the apocalypse outside is real. Masterful tension.

sections.content: The film's practical effects and CGI monsters hold up remarkably well, but it's the human horror that truly disturbs. Marcia Gay Harden's portrayal of Mrs. Carmody, a religious zealot who gains frightening influence over the trapped survivors, echoes similar explorations of faith gone wrong in films like The Witch (2015) and Saint Maud (2020). The supermarket setting becomes a microcosm of society breaking down, reminiscent of Lord of the Flies (1963) but with supernatural terror lurking in the fog. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Impact on Horror Cinema

Darabont's decision to shoot the film in a gritty, almost documentary style influenced later horror films like The Crazies (2010) and The Mist's spiritual successor The Walking Dead (2010-2022), which Darabont initially developed for television. The film's exploration of how quickly civilization can crumble under pressure shares DNA with 28 Days Later (2002) and The Divide (2011), while its cosmic horror elements draw from Lovecraftian traditions seen in In the Mouth of Madness (1994).
